builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
summary: Replaces standard low-bit weight quantization (e.g., GPTQ/AWQ-style calibration) with rotation-and-scaling outlier mitigation, clustering-based codebooks with per-layer adaptive bit allocation, and calibration samples matched to early reasoning decoding statistics. Costs implementation complexity: it depends on a custom LUT CUDA kernel, per-layer codebook tuning, and a calibration pipeline that must capture early-token activation states, plus lookup overhead that may not reach the reported speedup on all hardware. Can fail when reasoning activation distributions differ from the calibration data, when small model sizes make the LUT kernel overhead dominate, or when the custom kernel is unmaintained for the reader's deployment stack.
rationale: A 24 GB GPU strongly motivates low-precision reasoning inference, but the custom kernel and calibration dependence require validation on the reader's specific models and hardware before production adoption.
technique: Clustering-based LUT quantization with early-decoding calibration

claims.statement: Replaces standard low-bit weight quantization (e.g., GPTQ/AWQ-style calibration) with rotation-and-scaling outlier mitigation, clustering-based codebooks with per-layer adaptive bit allocation, and calibration samples matched to early reasoning decoding statistics. Costs implementation complexity: it depends on a custom LUT CUDA kernel, per-layer codebook tuning, and a calibration pipeline that must capture early-token activation states, plus lookup overhead that may not reach the reported speedup on all hardware. Can fail when reasoning activation distributions differ from the calibration data, when small model sizes make the LUT kernel overhead dominate, or when the custom kernel is unmaintained for the reader's deployment stack.
Delivers substantial accuracy improvements on reasoning benchmarks while achieving up to 2.85x speedup over BF16 via a customized LUT CUDA kernel.
